surfaces.part: grass and dark undergrowth at base

answer.evidence: The object is a 16px-wide, 64-row vertical cliff wall with a face-on stone texture, drawn as stacked blocks with dark crack lines. The only top-like feature is rows 1-3, a light band of L=160 that ends in a dark line at rows 3-4. That is a 2-3 row bevel or rim, not a horizontal surface with an eave. The white streak at rows 18-21 is a highlight on the vertical face and has no top plane above it. The silhouette is a constant 16 wide for all rows, so there is no ellipse, roof or canopy. Below row 47 the rock gives way to grass and dark foliage. It is a tall vertical face with no top surface and does not read as a large structure such as a gate, pavilion or building.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a narrow strip of grey rock face with a patch of dark vegetation at the bottom, not a building with roof, walls and door/windows, so it does not match the reference kind. It is also only about one tile wide. On the measured facts, it has 10 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, and 0% near-flat coverage, so the density is comparable. The weak point is the outline: 83% of dark edge pixels are near-neutral, against 7% and 9% for the references, which means a neutral dark line instead of a dark tone of the adjacent material. The rock reads as only about 4 grey steps with a few speckles, where the references have 5-6 steps with per-tile highlights and grain. Because the kind does not match and the outline is neutral, it falls short of the Beodeul standard.
